correctness.rationale: For P_q(z)=product_(j=0)^3(z-eta+j), differentiation gives periodic w' in ker L and scaling yields e^t(w'-eta w) in ker L; the last identity follows from P(D+1)(D-eta)=P(D)(D-eta+4) and 4+(q-1)eta=0. This was independently checked as a polynomial identity. The reflection P(z)=P(-sigma-z), sigma=3-2eta, was also independently verified, so L*=exp(sigma t)L exp(-sigma t). Adjoint monodromy inversion forces multiplier involution mu -> exp(-sigma T)/mu. Applying it to distinct 1 and exp(T) produces exp(-sigma T) and exp(-(sigma+1)T), exhausting order four with no overlaps for q>1,T>0. No numerical orbit computation is used to infer the universal claim.
residual_risks: No periodic orbit existence or uniqueness for every q>1 is proved; exact spectral identity is conditional.
Parameter limits q downarrow 1 are singular and excluded.

value.rationale: The exact spectrum gives the spectral half of a published explicit conjecture conditional on profile existence; it replaces orbit-specific Floquet numerics with an all-q algebraic law and determines the hyperbolic index. This is a nonstandard structural identity, not a numerical precision upgrade.
residual_risks: No construction of a periodic profile for every q or global blow-up classification follows.

final_claim: Conditional on a nonconstant T-periodic solution w of P_q(D)w+|w|^{q-1}w=0, q>1, eta=-4/(q-1), all Floquet exponents (on a common logarithm branch) are 0,1,-(3q+5)/(q-1),-4(q+1)/(q-1); the corresponding four multipliers are distinct.
limitations: Conditional on nonconstant periodic profile, q>1; no existence, uniqueness, basin or lower-order-perturbation theorem.
Literature search is not exhaustive and no external certification is asserted.
